implementation_notes: Foundation gives Swift a boolean-attempt lock: NSLock.try() 'attempts to acquire a lock and immediately returns a Boolean value that indicates whether the attempt was successful' instead of suspending, so the classic guarded method is a try() plus an early return under a defer-unlock, and DispatchSemaphore.wait(timeout: .now()) is the GCD equivalent of the same balk for semaphore-shaped state. Swift Concurrency has no blocking attempt - actors serialise by awaiting - so inside async code balking is an explicit isolated state check followed by an early return, or the guarded region is kept strictly synchronous on a thread.
pitfalls: NSLock.try() returns false when the same thread already owns the lock (NSLock is not recursive), so a nested guarded call balks and the work is silently skipped.
An await between the check and the state change lets another task interleave even though the guard looks synchronous - keep suspension points out of the guarded region.
DispatchSemaphore.wait(timeout: .now()) reports refusal as .timedOut, so ignoring the return value turns a balk into an accidental wait or a silent no-op.
